_conditions: All times in ns. Values transcribed from the cited manufacturer datasheets (downloaded Oct 2026). Per arc: 'max' = maximum propagation delay over -40..+85 C at CL = 50 pF and VCC = 4.5 V (HCT) or VCC = 5 V +-0.5 V (ACT, whose limits therefore cover 4.5 V). 'typ' = 25 C typical at VCC = 5 V: for HCT parts the datasheets only give the 5 V typical at CL = 15 pF, so HCT 'typ' is a 15 pF number and reads ~2-4 ns faster than a 50 pF load would give; 'typ_4V5_50pF' (25 C, 4.5 V, 50 pF) is the like-for-like HCT typical where the datasheet gives it (Nexperia and TI SN74HCT sheets). For ACT parts 'typ' is 25 C, 5 V, CL = 50 pF. 'min' = guaranteed minimum delay over -40..+85 C (only ACT sheets specify it; useful for hold checks). Where tPLH and tPHL differ, the larger value is given (and the smaller min). Enable = tPZH/tPZL, disable = tPHZ/tPLZ. 'checks' are datasheet minimum timing requirements over -40..+85 C at 4.5 V (HCT) or 5 V +-0.5 V (ACT); 'fmax_MHz' is the guaranteed minimum maximum clock frequency. A missing key means the datasheet does not give it. Keys ending in '_est' are estimates, explained in 'notes'. Pin names are normalised to TI style (CLK, /CLR, /LOAD, ENP, ENT, RCO, /OE, /G); each part's notes give the datasheet's own names where they differ. 'alt' lists second-source datasheets with their own numbers: vendors differ a lot, so for worst-case STA use the datasheet of the vendor you actually buy, or the worse of the two.

S0,S1->I/O enable_est.basis: NOT specified in any 299 datasheet found (TI CD74HCT299, NXP 74HCT299, TI CD74ACT299, Fairchild/onsemi 74ACT299): all give only OE->I/O enable/disable. All of them say S0 = S1 = H turns the I/O 3-state buffers off just like a high /OE1 or /OE2 (TI: 'regardless of the status of OE1 and OE2'), so the estimate is set equal to this datasheet's /OE->I/O time. Not a guaranteed bound: S0/S1 may pass through one more gate (mode decode) than /OE, so leave a few ns of margin, e.g. switch S0/S1 to load early in the cycle before the other bus driver turns on.

S0,S1->I/O disable_est.basis: NOT specified in any 299 datasheet found (TI CD74HCT299, NXP 74HCT299, TI CD74ACT299, Fairchild/onsemi 74ACT299): all give only OE->I/O enable/disable. All of them say S0 = S1 = H turns the I/O 3-state buffers off just like a high /OE1 or /OE2 (TI: 'regardless of the status of OE1 and OE2'), so the estimate is set equal to this datasheet's /OE->I/O time. Not a guaranteed bound: S0/S1 may pass through one more gate (mode decode) than /OE, so leave a few ns of margin, e.g. switch S0/S1 to load early in the cycle before the other bus driver turns on.

function_table./MR=L: asynchronous clear: Q0-Q7 = L, overrides S0, S1 and CP
function_table.S1=L S0=L: hold: register unchanged on the CP rising edge (TI 'Hold (do nothing)')
function_table.S1=L S0=H: shift right (TI/NXP/Fairchild name) = toward Q7: on CP rising edge DS0 -> Q0, Q0 -> Q1, ..., Q6 -> Q7
function_table.S1=H S0=L: shift left = toward Q0: on CP rising edge DS7 -> Q7, Q7 -> Q6, ..., Q1 -> Q0
function_table.S1=H S0=H: parallel load: on CP rising edge I/On -> Qn. The I/O output buffers are off (Z) in this mode whatever /OE1 and /OE2 are, so the I/O pins act as inputs

74HCT299.io_outputs: I/O0-I/O7 drive the register contents only when /OE1 = L and /OE2 = L and NOT (S0 = H and S1 = H). /OE1 = H or /OE2 = H -> Z. S0 = S1 = H -> Z regardless of /OE1, /OE2 (the pins become the parallel-load inputs). Shift, hold, load and clear still work while the I/O pins are Z. Q0 and Q7 are ordinary (non-3-state) serial outputs, always driven, unaffected by /OE1, /OE2, S0 and S1.
74HCT299.notes: Datasheet names: CP = CLK, MR (active low, /MR) = /CLR, OE1/OE2 (active low) = /OE (either one high disables), DS0 = serial input for shift right (toward Q7), DS7 = serial input for shift left (toward Q0), Q0/Q7 = serial outputs (other 299 datasheets call them Q0'/Q7' or QA'/QH'). '/' in 'pins' marks an overbar. TI gives one row for 'Clock to I/O Output, Clock to Q0 and Q7' (45 max at 25 C) and one row for 'MR to Output' (all outputs); MR has no 5 V/15 pF typical in the HCT section. The enable/disable typical is printed '10, 13, 15' for tPZL, tPZH/tPLZ, tPHZ (order taken from the HC rows of the same table), so enable typ = tPZH 13 and disable typ = tPHZ 15. Max: tPZH 40, tPZL 38; tPHZ 46, tPLZ 40. The HCT prerequisite table has two setup rows: 'DS0, DS7, I/On, S0, S1 to Clock' = 25 and 'S1, S0 to Clock' = 34; the specific (larger) 34 is used for S0/S1. tw CLK is not split into high and low. Vendor spread: the discontinued NXP part needs 31 ns data and 40 ns S0/S1 setup, but has a faster CLK->output (46). S0,S1->I/O _est arcs: see their basis.

74ACT299.datasheet: TI SCHS288A (Dec 1998, revised Dec 2024), covers CD54/74AC299, CD74AC323 and CD54/74ACT299; arcs from its 'Switching Characteristics, ACT Series'. Rev. A dropped the timing-requirements table, so 'checks' come from the previous revision SCHS288 (Harris-derived scan, TI PDF with package addendum dated 3 Mar 2022, table 'Prerequisite for switching: ACT series', p.257), read from the datasheet4u.com mirror in checks_source.
74ACT299.availability: Only one current maker: Texas Instruments, and only in SOIC. CD74ACT299M96 (SOIC-20, reel) is 'Active' in TI's package addendum (18 Sep 2026), plus military CD54ACT299F3A (CDIP). No plastic DIP; no SN74ACT299 exists (ti.com link 404s). Fairchild/onsemi 74ACT299 (SC/MTC/PC) is obsolete per DigiKey and other distributors, and DigiKey points to the TI part. onsemi still hosts MC74AC299/D Rev. 8 (Jun 2006), which lists MC74ACT299N/DW, but no orderable MC74ACT299 was found.
74ACT299.typ_cond: not given (TI's front page only quotes 'typical propagation delay 6 ns @ VCC = 5 V, 25 C, CL = 50 pF'; see 'alt' for Fairchild typicals)
74ACT299.max_cond: max/min: -40..+85 C, VCC 5 V +-0.5 V (i.e. covers 4.5 V), CL 50 pF; checks -40..+85 C, '5 V: min is @ 4.5 V'

S0,S1->I/O enable_est.basis: NOT specified in any 299 datasheet found (TI CD74HCT299, NXP 74HCT299, TI CD74ACT299, Fairchild/onsemi 74ACT299): all give only OE->I/O enable/disable. All of them say S0 = S1 = H turns the I/O 3-state buffers off just like a high /OE1 or /OE2 (TI: 'regardless of the status of OE1 and OE2'), so the estimate is set equal to this datasheet's /OE->I/O time. Not a guaranteed bound: S0/S1 may pass through one more gate (mode decode) than /OE, so leave a few ns of margin, e.g. switch S0/S1 to load early in the cycle before the other bus driver turns on.

S0,S1->I/O disable_est.basis: NOT specified in any 299 datasheet found (TI CD74HCT299, NXP 74HCT299, TI CD74ACT299, Fairchild/onsemi 74ACT299): all give only OE->I/O enable/disable. All of them say S0 = S1 = H turns the I/O 3-state buffers off just like a high /OE1 or /OE2 (TI: 'regardless of the status of OE1 and OE2'), so the estimate is set equal to this datasheet's /OE->I/O time. Not a guaranteed bound: S0/S1 may pass through one more gate (mode decode) than /OE, so leave a few ns of margin, e.g. switch S0/S1 to load early in the cycle before the other bus driver turns on.

function_table./MR=L: asynchronous clear: Q0-Q7 = L, overrides S0, S1 and CP
function_table.S1=L S0=L: hold: register unchanged on the CP rising edge (TI 'Hold (do nothing)')
function_table.S1=L S0=H: shift right (TI/NXP/Fairchild name) = toward Q7: on CP rising edge DS0 -> Q0, Q0 -> Q1, ..., Q6 -> Q7
function_table.S1=H S0=L: shift left = toward Q0: on CP rising edge DS7 -> Q7, Q7 -> Q6, ..., Q1 -> Q0
function_table.S1=H S0=H: parallel load: on CP rising edge I/On -> Qn. The I/O output buffers are off (Z) in this mode whatever /OE1 and /OE2 are, so the I/O pins act as inputs

74ACT299.io_outputs: I/O0-I/O7 drive the register contents only when /OE1 = L and /OE2 = L and NOT (S0 = H and S1 = H). /OE1 = H or /OE2 = H -> Z. S0 = S1 = H -> Z regardless of /OE1, /OE2 (the pins become the parallel-load inputs). Shift, hold, load and clear still work while the I/O pins are Z. Q0 and Q7 are ordinary (non-3-state) serial outputs, always driven, unaffected by /OE1, /OE2, S0 and S1.
74ACT299.notes: Datasheet names: CP = CLK, MR (active low, /MR) = /CLR, OE1/OE2 (active low) = /OE, DS0/DS7 = serial inputs (shift right toward Q7 / shift left toward Q0), Q0/Q7 = serial outputs (Q0'/Q7' elsewhere). The Rev. A pin table misprints S0 and DS0 as 'SO' and 'DSO'. TI gives a single 'Enable and Disable Times' row (tPLZ, tPHZ, tPZL, tPZH) and separate MR->Q0,Q7 and MR->I/On rows; arc 'min' is at 5.5 V. The old TI table's -55..+125 C column: S0/S1 setup 9, data setup 4.5, tw CLK 5.5, tw MR 5, recovery 5, fmax 90 MHz (the 90 MHz on TI's product page). Vendor spread: TI needs 7.9 ns S0/S1 setup and 4.4 ns MR recovery but 0 ns hold, while Fairchild/onsemi need 5.5 ns S0/S1 setup and 1.5 ns recovery but 1.0 ns hold on every input; for a part of unknown origin use the worse of the two (S setup 7.9, DS setup 5.0, I/O setup 4.5, hold 1.0, recovery 4.4). S0,S1->I/O _est arcs: see their basis.

Per edge (typ/max): CLK->Q0,Q7 tPLH 8.5/14.0, tPHL 9.0/15.0; CLK->I/O tPLH 8.5/13.5, tPHL 9.5/16.5; MR gives tPHL only; enable tPZH 8.0/13.0, tPZL 8.0/13.5; disable tPHZ 8.5/13.5, tPLZ 8.0/12.5. The 25 C typical of MR->Q0,Q7 (14.0) is printed close to its 25 C max (15.0). tw CLK is HIGH or LOW.
